title: Webtopia Alternatives for Ad Creative and Meta Campaigns
summary: Webtopia alternatives compared: Knowlify for finished AI video ads, plus agencies with published prices, channels and fit notes, checked October 2026.
body_markdown:
## Which agencies suit a multichannel or larger budget?


**Darkroom: fit for multichannel consumer brands.** As of October 2026, Darkroom says its fit is mid-market and enterprise consumer brands, typically $10M to $500M in revenue, and poor for single-channel brands and companies under roughly $5M. Its paid media page lists pricing as a retainer plus a percentage of media, from $1,500 a month. Its performance creative service lists 250 to 600 production-ready assets per cycle, delivered every two weeks ([Darkroom paid media page](https://darkroomagency.com/services/paid-media) ).


**Pilothouse: fit for established DTC ecommerce.** As of October 2026, Pilothouse says it is built for established DTC ecommerce brands, that most of its clients are based in North America, and that it prices through monthly retainers, performance incentives and custom scopes. No minimum spend is published, and onboarding typically begins within 5 to 10 business days of signing ([Pilothouse homepage](https://www.pilothouse.co/) ).


**NoGood: fit for larger retainers.** As of October 2026, NoGood says its average monthly retainer is above $20,000, it has no standardized packages, and it is headquartered in New York. Its paid social page covers Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, Reddit, LinkedIn, Snapchat, X and YouTube ([NoGood homepage](https://nogood.io/) ). For a wider shortlist of Meta-focused agencies, see[best performance marketing agencies for Meta](https://knowlify.com/articles/best-performance-marketing-agencies-meta) .


## What changes for a UK brand?


Webtopia is based in London, so a UK buyer may care about time zones, invoicing and where the team sits. Knowlify is based in San Francisco and works remotely with US brands, so a UK team should confirm approval hours before choosing it. As of October 2026, Creative Milkshake lists hubs in Amsterdam, London, Paris, Berlin, Dublin and Stockholm, and makes ads in seven languages, including English. It publishes no pricing, minimums or turnaround ([Creative Milkshake](https://www.creativemilkshake.com/performance-creative-agency) ).


inBeat's FAQ says it works remotely and adjusts to each client's time zone. It does not publish pricing ([inBeat performance creative page](https://inbeat.agency/performance-creative-agency) ). Ask any remote agency how approvals run across time zones before you sign.


## What should you ask before you switch?


- **Channels.** Is the work Meta only, or Meta plus Google and Amazon? Knowlify covers Meta video only.
- **Volume.** How many distinct concepts a month, counted separately from resizes and hook swaps?
- **Ad accounts.** Who owns the account? Meta's documentation says only the business that owns an ad account can add an agency to it, and the grant lists the tasks the agency may perform, so keep the account in your own business ([Meta business asset management guide](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/business-management-apis/business-asset-management/guides/business-to-business) ).
- **AI labels.** Meta says it labels ads with photorealistic AI-generated people made with its own tools. It says it will detect ads made with third-party AI tools and show an AI info label, but its post does not say that detection is live yet ([Meta's AI transparency update](https://about.fb.com/news/2025/02/gen-ai-transparency-metas-ads-products/) ).


## Key takeaways


- Knowlify is our top pick for finished AI video ads on Meta, with about 25 finished ads a week and a person checking each one.
- Foreplay's listing puts Webtopia's work across Meta, Google and Amazon, and it is our only source for that, so confirm the scope in writing.
- Darkroom publishes a starting retainer and Pilothouse publishes fit notes, which makes them easier to compare than agencies that publish nothing.
- NoGood fits larger retainers, with an average above $20,000 a month.
- Ask every option which channels it covers, how many concepts it makes, and who owns the ad accounts.


## FAQ


### What is the best Webtopia alternative?


Knowlify is our top pick if you need finished AI video ads for Meta and do not need a full media retainer. It makes about 25 ads a week, and a person checks every one. If you also need Google work, shortlist Darkroom or Pilothouse and request a written scope.


### Does Knowlify run Google Ads?


No. Knowlify does not run Google, TikTok, LinkedIn or YouTube ads. Its service is video ads for Facebook and Instagram, with optional Meta campaign management.


### Which Webtopia alternative publishes prices?


As of October 2026, Darkroom publishes a retainer starting at $1,500 a month plus a percentage of media. Most others in this list publish no per-project price. NoGood gives only an average retainer, above $20,000 a month, so request a written quote on the same brief.


### How does Meta label AI-generated people in ads?


Meta labels photorealistic AI-generated people made with its own creative tools, and the label sits next to Sponsored. It says it will detect third-party AI tools and show an AI info label, but its post does not say that is live yet. Plan for the label in your approvals.


### Should I keep the ad account if I switch agencies?


Yes. Keep the account in your business and grant each agency only the tasks it needs. Meta's documentation says only the owning business can add an agency, so changing agencies then means changing access, not rebuilding campaigns from scratch.
